messages:
jonathan: Heads up — after enabling FP8 on the L40S canary cluster I'm seeing sporadic token latency spikes (2–3x) that start ~120s into long-chat sessions. Repro with batch shape 1x8, microbatch 1, seq_len 2048.

sophie: which kernel is the runtime picking when this happens? TE fp8 or an int8 fallback?

jonathan: at first it's TE fp8-path, then mid-episode it flips to int8_slowpath. Quick stack snippet from the node: 
```text
kernel: te_fp8_rowwise
fallback: int8_attention_slow
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.12 -> 0.00
batch_shape: 1x8
latency p95: 320ms -> 780ms
```

maya: 12% hit rate is rough. Did we change any KV eviction params recently?

jonathan: yes — last week we bumped KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD to 0.65 in canary to reduce memory pressure.

raj: can you attach the profiler traces (raptor/torchprof) and the transformer-engine env? Also include the kernel selection decision logs (we emit kernel_reason).

jonathan: here's an excerpt from the perf dump (sanitized):
```text
2026-03-15T16:12:04Z pid=4221 select_kernel: cost_te=120, cost_int8_slow=60 -> choose te_fp8
2026-03-15T16:12:20Z pid=4221 select_kernel: cost_te=480, cost_int8_slow=70 -> choose int8_attention_slow (fallback)
KV cache miss-rate: 88%
DMA stalls: 40%
memcpy bandwidth collapse observed on host-03
```

infra-bot: deploy event — canary/l40s fp8-guard-3 rolled at 2026-03-15T16:00:00Z by ci/cd

sophie: hypothesis: continuous batching + KV eviction => cache churn => spike in TE execution time (more memcpy / cache misses) -> cost model thinks te_fp8 more expensive and routes to int8_slowpath. Could also be PCIe/thermal throttling on that node causing memcpy slowdowns.

maya: quick repro steps I used: run long-chat generator with seed=4932, context=6k, batch=1x8, precompile_warmup=false. If you hit p95 > 600ms, capture /tmp/trace_* and profiler snapshot. I also toggled KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD back to 0.5 and saw fewer fallbacks.

raj: micro-bench results I ran locally (L40S mock):
```text
shape 1x8 len 2048: te_fp8_rowwise p99 = 210ms
shape 1x8 len 4096: te_fp8 p99 = 300ms
shape 1x8 len 2048 + kv_churn: fallback int8 p99 = 720ms
```

jonathan: action items I'm proposing: (1) revert KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD to 0.5 on canary now; (2) force TE kernel selection on one L40S host (TE_FORCE_FP8=1) to A/B; (3) collect HW perf counters (PCIe/SM throughput) for the bad host. @sophie @maya can you own 1 & 2?

sophie: on it — reverting KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD on canary. Also adding more telemetry: kernel_reason and kv_miss_rate tags on request spans so we can correlate. :white_check_mark:

maya: I'll provision a debug node with TE_FORCE_FP8=1 and run the long-chat harness A/B against the reverted config.

raj: I'll take the perf traces and try a narrow bisect on the cost model (where it increments the TE estimated time). Suspect a calibration/scale update in fp8 runtime that increases memcpy or reduces compute packing efficiency under certain sequence-length distributions.

jonathan: also note — H100 hasn't shown this pattern in our quick runs, but we need an H100 long-context run to be sure it's platform-specific. Sophie, can you queue an H100 canary test after the L40S repro?

sophie: queued H100 run now. will report results in this thread.

jonathan: thanks everyone. small follow-up: if the KV eviction revert stabilizes latency we'll ship a temporary guard until we fix cost-estimation and add early detection.

maya: FYI I captured a host trace and uploaded to /shared/debug/fp8_l40s_host03_trace.tar.gz (link: https://internal.redwood/s/fp8_trace). contains raptor traces, nvprof snapshots, and kernel selection logs.

raj: perfect — i'll start the bisect with that trace. might add a fast heuristic: if kv_miss_rate > 50% prefer te_int8_fastpath over te_fp8 to avoid slow memcpy spikes while we fix calibration.

jonathan: :thumbsup: ping me if you need more capacity on canary or a quick rollback.

sophie: preliminary L40S A/B after revert shows p95 down from ~720ms to ~260ms on the canary group. H100 run still shows stable te_fp8.

jonathan: great, leave the revert in place and let's run a small-scale dogfood for 24h, then iterate on the cost model and telemetry.
